## Preliminaries

**Working scope (declared as assumption, not fact).** Mic 3:1-12 is taken as a single reading unit: a direct, first-person indictment of Israel's/Jacob's own "heads and rulers" for violently exploiting their people (vv1-4), a matching indictment of hireling false prophets (vv5-7), Micah's own contrasting self-declaration of genuine prophetic empowerment (v8), and a recapitulating, escalated final charge against heads/priests/prophets together, closing with the devastating verdict against Zion/Jerusalem/the temple mount itself (vv9-12). "Bearing on the inner being" includes: (i) Micah himself, speaking throughout in first person ("I said," v1; "as for me, I am filled," v8) — his most direct, sustained personal presence in the book so far; (ii) "the heads of Jacob and rulers of the house of Israel" — the chapter's primary guilty party, given explicit stated moral inversion (v2) and violent metaphor (vv2-3); (iii) "my people," their victims; (iv) the false prophets, motivated explicitly by payment (v5); (v) the LORD, both refusing to answer the rulers' cry (v4) and withdrawing the prophets' own vision (v6-7); (vi) "its heads... its priests... its prophets" together (v11), all three offices named as corrupt, yet claiming false confidence in divine protection.

**Reading rule applied.** No [AMBIGUOUS]-span STEP-live resolution was needed — the base extract reports 100% meaning coverage for this range (140/140 non-particle spans). Register: first-person prophetic address opening the chapter ("And I said," v1, distinct from Mic 1's third-person "the word... came" and closer to Mic 2's direct address), extended visceral metaphor (vv2-3), narrated verdict (v4), divine oracle formula introducing a second indictment (v5), further verdict (vv6-7), a first-person self-declaration (v8, unique in the book so far), and a closing recapitulation-plus-verdict (vv9-12).

**Corpus-continuity check.** Immediately-adjacent prior range, found automatically: `Mic 2:1-13` — `iba\app\verse-analysis\Micah\WA-mic-2-debate.md`. Read in full before drafting this debate. Carried forward: the divine-possessive "my people" pattern (Mic 2:4, 8, 9, now recurring at v5); the false-prophet/false-confidence controversy (Mic 2:6, 11, now recurring almost verbatim at v11 — "disgrace will not overtake us" / "no disaster shall come upon us"); the "fields"/land vocabulary (Mic 2:2, 4, now recurring at v12's climactic "Zion shall be plowed as a field").

## Per-verse debate

### Mic 3:1

> And I said: Hear, you heads of Jacob and rulers of the house of Israel! Is it not for you to know justice?—

**Observation.** "And I said [H0559]: Hear [H8085G], you heads [H7218H] of Jacob [H3290] and rulers [H7101] of the house [H1004M] of Israel [H3478]! Is it not [H3808] for you to know [H3045] justice [H4941H]?"

**Operation 1 — Micah's own direct, first-person challenge to Israel's ruling class.**
- **Action-type:** challenged (a direct rhetorical question, implying its own negative-but-expected answer: they do NOT, despite their office, know justice).
- **Subject:** Micah, speaking in first person ("I said" — a more direct, personal register than Mic 1's third-person "the word... came"); "the heads of Jacob and rulers of the house of Israel," directly addressed and challenged by office/title.
- **Operation:** a state — a rhetorical challenge naming their own explicit professional duty (to know/administer justice) as the very thing they are about to be shown failing at.
- **Source:** self — Micah's own direct address.
- **Target:** "the heads... and rulers," challenged by their own office.

**Interrogative — questions considered.**
- Q1/Q2: The heads/rulers — directly addressed by title, given a stated professional duty (knowing justice) that the rest of the chapter will show them violating.
- Q3: Stated explicitly, via direct rhetorical question.
- Q4: Source = Micah, self, explicit — his most direct personal presence in the book so far.
- Q5: Target = the heads/rulers.
- Q6: State (the rhetorical challenge).
- Q7: Forward linkage to the whole chapter — this verse names the office (justice) that vv2-3 will show being violently betrayed.
- Q8: "Heads of Jacob," "rulers of the house of Israel" — a ruling-class collective, named by title/office rather than by locale (contrast Mic 1's town-by-town address).
- Q9: Sufficient for what is stated.
- Q11: challenged.

**Decision.** Retain — the chapter's opening direct address, naming the very office (justice) the following verses will show violated.

### Mic 3:2

> you who hate the good and love the evil, who tear the skin from off my people and their flesh from off their bones,

**Observation.** "You who hate [H8130] the good [H2896B] and love [H0157G] the evil [H7451B], who tear [H1497] the skin [H5785] from off [H5921A/H9006] my people [note: continuing address, "them"] and their flesh [H7607] from off their bones [H6106G]."

**Operation 1 — the rulers' own stated moral inversion, and the violent metaphor of flaying their own people.**
- **Action-type:** hated-good/loved-evil (a directly stated, complete moral inversion — the clearest possible statement of corrupted interior orientation); tore/flayed (a violent metaphor for systemic exploitation).
- **Subject:** the heads/rulers of v1, continuing as addressed subject; their victims (implied "my people," made explicit at v3), whose skin and flesh are torn away.
- **Operation:** a state — a directly named, complete moral inversion (hating what is good, loving what is evil — not merely doing wrong, but having reordered their own affections); a movement — the violent, physical metaphor of flaying, standing for economic/social exploitation so severe it is imaged as literal bodily violence.
- **Source:** self — the rulers' own inverted affections, explicit.
- **Target:** "my people" — their own victims, whose skin/flesh/bones are the object of this violence.

**Interrogative — questions considered.**
- Q1/Q2: The rulers — given the chapter's most direct possible statement of inverted moral interior (hating good, loving evil), not inferred from conduct but named as the affection itself.
- Q3: Stated explicitly.
- Q4: Source = the rulers' own affections, self, explicit.
- Q5: Target = their own people, described in the most visceral possible terms.
- Q6: State (the inverted affections) and movement (the violent metaphor).
- Q7: Direct forward linkage to v3 (the metaphor's continuation and escalation into full butchery/cooking imagery).
- Q8: "My people" — the whole victim-collective, continuing the divine-possessive pattern already tracked across this study.
- Q9: Sufficient for what is stated.
- Q11: hated/loved (inverted affections); tore/flayed (violent exploitation, metaphorical).

**Decision.** Retain — one of the clearest direct statements of inverted moral interior in the book, paired with its own visceral metaphor.

### Mic 3:3

> who eat the flesh of my people, and flay their skin from off them, and break their bones in pieces and chop them up like meat in a pot, like flesh in a cauldron.

**Observation.** "Who eat [H0398] the flesh [H7607] of my people [H5971A], and flay [H6584] their skin [H5785] from off them, and break [H6476] their bones [H6106G] in pieces, and chop [H6566] them up like [H9004] meat in a pot [H5518A], like [H9004] flesh [H1320] in the midst [H8432] of a cauldron [H7037]."

**Operation 1 — the extended cannibalism-butchery metaphor, at its most explicit.**
- **Action-type:** ate/flayed/broke/chopped (a four-verb escalation, the most graphic sustained metaphor for exploitation in the book so far).
- **Subject:** the same rulers, continuing directly from v2; "my people," their victims, described now not merely as flayed but consumed, butchered, and cooked — a complete, systematic devouring.
- **Operation:** a movement — total, methodical consumption, likened explicitly to preparing meat for a meal (pot, cauldron) — the rulers' exploitation imaged as literally living off their own people's substance.
- **Source:** self — the rulers, continuing v2's stated inverted affections into fully enacted violence.
- **Target:** "my people" — their skin, flesh, and bones, the totality of the metaphorical victim's body.

**Interrogative — questions considered.**
- Q1/Q2: The rulers — the metaphor's escalation itself is a form of stated interior content: not merely disliking or neglecting their people but consuming them, an image of total, appetitive exploitation.
- Q3: Stated explicitly, via direct, extended metaphor.
- Q4: Source = the rulers, self, continuing v2.
- Q5: Target = "my people," their whole body (skin, flesh, bones) — a totalizing image of complete exploitation.
- Q6: Movement throughout (eating, flaying, breaking, chopping).
- Q7: Direct continuation of v2; together vv2-3 form the chapter's most sustained single metaphor, structurally parallel to (though far more violent than) Mic 1's animal-cry mourning imagery (jackals/ostriches, Mic 1:8) — both instances of the book reaching for vivid, non-literal imagery to convey what plain statement alone would not.
- Q8: "My people" — the whole victim-collective.
- Q9: Sufficient for what is stated.
- Q11: consumed/butchered (continuing and completing v2's tore/flayed).

**Decision.** Retain — the chapter's most graphic sustained metaphor, directly grounding v4's coming verdict.

### Mic 3:4

> Then they will cry to the Lord, but he will not answer them; he will hide his face from them at that time, because they have made their deeds evil.

**Observation.** "Then [H0227A] they will cry [H2199] to [H0413] the LORD [H3068G], but he will not [H3808] answer [H6030B] them; he will hide [H5641] his face [H6440H] from them at that time [H6256], because [H0834A] they have made their deeds evil [H7489A]."

**Operation 1 — the rulers' own future cry for help, met with the LORD's silence and hidden face.**
- **Action-type:** cried/was-refused (a stated future reversal: those who devoured their own people's cries — implied, not stated, but the natural counterpart to vv2-3's victims — will themselves cry out and receive the same silence).
- **Subject:** the rulers, continuing as addressed subject; the LORD, explicitly named as the one who will not answer.
- **Operation:** a movement — their own future crying out; a state — the LORD's declared, deliberate non-response and hidden face.
- **Source:** the rulers' own prior conduct, explicitly named as the cause ("because they have made their deeds evil") — a direct, stated causal link, not merely juxtaposed.
- **Target:** n/a directly — the rulers' own cry, met with silence, reflexively their own consequence.

**Interrogative — questions considered.**
- Q1/Q2: The rulers — given a stated future interior act (crying out, presumably in distress) that will go unanswered; a genuine, if brief, moment of vulnerability for the very party that showed none to others.
- Q3: Stated explicitly, both the future cry and its refusal.
- Q4: Source = the rulers' own prior "evil deeds," explicitly named as cause; the LORD's refusal itself sourced to self, explicit.
- Q5: Target = n/a directly, reflexive.
- Q6: Movement (crying out) and state (the LORD's deliberate non-response).
- Q7: A structural (not lexically-anchored) parallel worth naming: the rulers showed no responsiveness to "my people's" own suffering (vv2-3, implied); the LORD now shows the identical non-responsiveness to THEM — a real thematic mirroring, though without a shared verb/root anchoring it as a formal Q12 instance (contrast Mic 2:1/3's clean "devise"/"devise" anchor) — named here as a linkage, not asserted as Q12.
- Q8: N/A — the rulers addressed as a collective, but the cry/refusal is described generically ("they"/"them"), not with collective-specific detail.
- Q9: Sufficient for what is stated.
- Q11: cried/was-refused.

**Decision.** Retain — a genuine consequence-verdict, directly and explicitly causal from the preceding metaphor; the structural (non-lexical) parallel to the rulers' own withheld compassion is named as a linkage, not overstated as a formal Q12 anchor.

### Mic 3:5

> Thus says the Lord concerning the prophets who lead my people astray, who cry “ Peace ” when they have something to eat, but declare war against him who puts nothing into their mouths.

**Observation.** "Thus says [H0559] the LORD [H3068G] concerning the prophets [H5030] who lead my people [H5971A] astray [H8582], who cry [H7121I] 'Peace' [H7965G] when they have something to bite [H5391A/H9020], but declare war [H4421/H6942J] against him who puts [H5414G] nothing [H3808/H0834A] into their mouths [H6310G]."

**Operation 1 — the false prophets' pay-determined message, opening a second indictment.**
- **Action-type:** led-astray/pronounced-peace-or-war (a stated corrupt motive: the prophetic verdict — blessing or curse — determined entirely by whether the prophet is fed).
- **Subject:** "the prophets," a distinct guilty party from vv1-4's rulers, introduced by a fresh divine-oracle formula ("thus says the LORD"); "my people," again their victims (the divine-possessive pattern, continuing).
- **Operation:** a state — corrupted prophetic motive, explicitly named; a movement — "leading astray," an active misdirection of the people's own trust.
- **Source:** self — the prophets' own venality, explicit.
- **Target:** "my people," misled; "him who puts nothing into their mouths" — a further specific victim, whoever fails to pay is cursed rather than blessed.

**Interrogative — questions considered.**
- Q1/Q2: The prophets — given directly stated, explicit corrupt motive: their own oracles determined by payment, not truth.
- Q3: Stated explicitly, via direct divine oracle.
- Q4: Source = the prophets' own venality, self, explicit.
- Q5: Target = "my people" (misled); the unpaying individual (cursed).
- Q6: State (corrupted motive) and movement (active misleading).
- Q7: Direct linkage to Mic 2:11 (the people's own preference for a lying preacher promising "wine and strong drink") — a second, closely related instance of prophecy-for-appetite, now made explicit as the prophets' OWN motive rather than merely the people's preference.
- Q8: "My people" — continuing the divine-possessive pattern (now a further instance across Mic 1:9, Mic 2:4/8/9, Mic 3:5).
- Q9: Sufficient for what is stated.
- Q11: led-astray/pronounced-for-pay.

**Decision.** Retain — a second, distinct guilty party (prophets, distinct from rulers), and a further divine-possessive instance.

### Mic 3:8

> But as for me, I am filled with power, with the Spirit of the Lord, and with justice and might, to declare to Jacob his transgression and to Israel his sin.

**Observation.** "But as for me [H0199], I [H0595] am filled [H4390] with power [H3581B], with the Spirit [H7307G] of the LORD [H3068G], and with justice [H4941H] and might [H1369], to declare [H5046] to Jacob [H3290] his transgression [H6588] and to Israel [H3478] his sin [H2403B]."

**Operation 1 — Micah's own direct, first-person declaration of genuine prophetic empowerment.**
- **Action-type:** was-filled/declared (a direct, explicit self-statement of empowerment — the chapter's, and so far the book's, clearest and most sustained first-person interior content).
- **Subject:** Micah, in emphatic first person ("but AS FOR ME, I..." — a deliberate contrastive construction, directly opposing himself to vv5-7's hireling prophets).
- **Operation:** a state — being filled: power, the Spirit of the LORD, justice, and might, named together as the genuine source of true prophecy, contrasted point-by-point against the false prophets' venal, empty vision; a movement — the resulting act, declaring Jacob's/Israel's own sin plainly, without regard for payment.
- **Source:** self, yet explicitly attributed — "the Spirit of the LORD" is named as the filling agent, an unusually direct statement of divine enablement of the prophet's own interior capacity (Part B.5's distinction directly and unusually explicitly bridged: the state itself — being filled — is sourced externally, to the LORD's own Spirit, not left ambiguous).
- **Target:** Jacob/Israel — declared their transgression/sin, directly, plainly.

**Interrogative — questions considered.**
- Q1/Q2: Micah — the chapter's, and the book's so far, most direct and sustained first-person statement of interior content: being filled, empowered, equipped — not inferred from an act but stated as the ground of the act itself.
- Q3: Stated explicitly, first person, emphatic.
- Q4: Source = explicitly named as "the Spirit of the LORD" — an unusually direct case where the text itself sources an interior capacity (being filled with power/justice/might) to divine enablement, not merely human self-assertion.
- Q5: Target = Jacob/Israel, told their own transgression/sin plainly.
- Q6: State (being filled) and movement (declaring).
- Q7: **Major linkage — the chapter's structural centre.** Directly, deliberately contrasts with vv5-7's hireling prophets (filled with nothing but appetite for payment, versus Micah's filling with the Spirit); also directly answers Mic 1:1's "which he saw" and Mic 3:1's "I said," now intensified into full self-declared empowerment.
- Q8: N/A — Micah addressed as an individual.
- Q9: Sufficient for what is stated.
- Q11: was-filled/declared.

**Decision.** Retain — the chapter's structural and theological centre: Micah's own genuine empowerment, directly contrasted against the false prophets just indicted, and the clearest first-person interior statement in the book to this point.

### Mic 3:11

> Its heads give judgment for a bribe; its priests teach for a price; its prophets practice divination for money; yet they lean on the Lord and say, “Is not the Lord in the midst of us? No disaster shall come upon us.”

**Observation.** "Its heads [H7218H] give judgment [H8199] for a bribe [H7810]; its priests [H3548] teach [H3384B] for a price [H4242]; its prophets [H5030] practice divination [H7080] for money [H3701G]; yet they lean [H8172] on the LORD [H3068G] and say [H0559]: 'Is not [H3808] the LORD [H3068G] in the midst [H7130G] of us? No [H3808] disaster [H7451C] shall come [H0935G] upon us.'"

**Operation 1 — three offices (heads, priests, prophets), all corrupt-for-pay, yet claiming false confidence in the LORD's own protection.**
- **Action-type:** judged/taught/divined-for-pay (three parallel corrupt offices, each named with its own specific currency of corruption); leaned/presumed (a stated false confidence, directly quoted).
- **Subject:** "its heads," "its priests," "its prophets" — three distinct leadership offices, all named together as corrupt, a total institutional indictment (widening from v5's prophets-alone charge and v1/9's heads/rulers-alone charge into all three at once).
- **Operation:** a state — systemic corruption across every office of leadership; a state — an explicit, quoted claim of false security, presuming the LORD's own presence guarantees safety regardless of their own conduct.
- **Source:** self — each office's own venality, explicit; their false confidence likewise self-sourced, a direct misapplication of genuine covenant theology (the LORD's real presence, elsewhere a true comfort) to excuse ongoing corruption.

**Interrogative — questions considered.**
- Q1/Q2: All three offices — given directly stated, explicit corrupt motive, paralleling the structure across heads/priests/prophets; their quoted claim is a genuine, stated (not inferred) interior confidence, though a false one.
- Q3: Stated explicitly throughout, including via direct quotation.
- Q4: Source = each office's own venality, self, explicit; the false confidence likewise self-sourced.
- Q5: Target = n/a for the corruption; reflexive for the presumed safety.
- Q6: State throughout.
- Q7: **Major cross-chapter linkage.** "No disaster shall come upon us" directly, almost verbatim, repeats Mic 2:6's false prophets' own denial ("disgrace will not overtake us") — the SAME underlying self-deception (confident denial of coming judgment, held by the very parties responsible for it) recurring within the same book, now widened from prophets alone to all three offices together.
- Q8: "Its heads," "its priests," "its prophets" — three distinct professional collectives, treated together as one composite guilty institution.
- Q9: Sufficient for what is stated.
- Q11: corrupted-for-pay (three offices); presumed-safety (their shared false confidence).

**Decision.** Retain — the chapter's fullest institutional indictment, and a direct, strong cross-chapter linkage to Mic 2:6's identical false-confidence pattern.

### Mic 3:12

> Therefore because of you Zion shall be plowed as a field; Jerusalem shall become a heap of ruins, and the mountain of the house a wooded height.

**Observation.** "Therefore because of [H1558] you Zion [H6726] shall be plowed [H2790A] as a field [H7704G]; Jerusalem [H3389] shall become a heap of ruins [H5856], and the mountain [H2022G] of the house [H1004B] shall become a wooded [H3293A] height [H1116]."

**Operation 1 — the chapter's climactic verdict: Zion plowed, Jerusalem ruined, the temple mount reduced to wilderness.**
- **Action-type:** plowed/ruined/reduced-to-wilderness (the most severe verdict in the book so far — not merely a city's judgment but the reduction of the LORD's own temple mount to unworked, wooded high ground).
- **Subject:** an unnamed agent (grammatically passive throughout — "shall be plowed," "shall become"), continuing the LORD's own declared judgment from vv4/6; Zion, Jerusalem, "the mountain of the house" (the temple mount, explicitly named), the direct objects of this reversal.
- **Operation:** a movement — total reversal: the built city (v10's "build Zion... Jerusalem") undone into plowed field and ruin-heap; the temple mount itself, the single most sacred site in the whole book's world, reduced to unworked wooded highland.
- **Source:** "because of you" — explicitly, directly attributed to the guilty parties named throughout the chapter (heads, priests, prophets), not an arbitrary or unexplained judgment.
- **Target:** Zion, Jerusalem, the temple mount — the totality of the nation's religious and political centre.

**Interrogative — questions considered.**
- Q1/Q2: The guilty parties (heads/priests/prophets, vv1-11) — the verse's grammatical subject is passive/the cities themselves, but the CAUSE is explicitly, directly attributed to them ("because of you").
- Q3: Stated explicitly, direct declarative verdict.
- Q4: Source = explicitly "because of you" — the chapter's guilty parties, named directly as the cause of this most severe of verdicts.
- Q5: Target = Zion, Jerusalem, the temple mount.
- Q6: Movement — total reversal of built city into plowed field/wooded ruin.
- Q7: **Major linkage, chapter-bracketing and cross-chapter.** Directly reverses v10 ("who BUILD Zion with blood" → "Zion shall be PLOWED as a field," the same city, its construction undone); directly continues the "field" (H7704G) vocabulary already tracked from Mic 2:2/4 (fields coveted, then lost) — now escalated to the whole holy city itself becoming agricultural/wild land; directly answers v11's false confidence ("no disaster shall come upon us") with the most severe disaster in the book so far.
- Q8: N/A — the cities/temple mount as objects, not human collectives.
- Q9: Sufficient for what is stated; this verse's own later citation elsewhere in the prophetic corpus (outside this base extract's own data) is not asserted here — named as a forward-pointer for when that portion of the corpus is read, not imported now.
- Q11: plowed/ruined/reduced-to-wilderness.

**Decision.** Retain — the chapter's climactic verdict, directly reversing v10's "building" charge and continuing the "field" vocabulary from Mic 2; the verse's own further significance elsewhere in the canon is flagged as a forward-pointer, not asserted from outside this base extract.

## Passage-level linkages (Q7)

1. **The heads/rulers thread (vv1, 9-12)**: v1's rhetorical question ("is it not for you to know justice?") is directly escalated at v9 ("who detest justice") and reaches its climax at v12 (the city they built on blood/iniquity, v10, undone into field and ruin) — one continuous, escalating charge bracketing the whole chapter.
2. **The prophets thread (vv5-7)**: corrupt, pay-determined oracles (v5) directly answered by withdrawn vision (v6) and public disgrace/silenced mouths (v7) — a self-contained judgment unit, structurally parallel to but distinct from the heads/rulers' own judgment (v4).
3. **Micah's own contrast (v8)**: positioned deliberately between the two indicted parties (rulers, vv1-4; prophets, vv5-7) and the recapitulation (vv9-12), Micah's own first-person filling with the LORD's Spirit stands as the chapter's positive counter-example to both surrounding indictments.
4. **The "field" (H7704G) vocabulary, cross-chapter**: Mic 2:2 (fields coveted/seized) → Mic 2:4 (fields lost, reallocated) → Mic 3:12 (Zion itself plowed AS a field) — an escalating use of the same term, from stolen farmland to the holy city's own total agricultural reduction.
5. **The false-confidence pattern, cross-chapter, near-verbatim**: Mic 2:6 ("disgrace will not overtake us") and Mic 3:11 ("no disaster shall come upon us") — the same underlying self-deception, now stated by name across two different chapters and two different (though overlapping) guilty parties.
6. **The divine-possessive "my people" pattern, continuing**: v2/3 (implied), v5 (explicit) — further instances alongside Mic 1:9, Mic 2:4/8/9.
7. **A structural (non-lexical) parallel of withheld response**: v4 (the LORD will not answer the rulers' own cry) and v7 (no answer from God for the prophets) — the same underlying pattern (withheld divine response, directly following withheld human compassion/false confidence) recurring twice within one chapter, without a single shared verb anchoring both instances as a formal Q12 pair — named as a linkage, not overstated.

## Insufficiencies register

- Whether v4's withheld divine response is intended as a direct, lexically-anchored answer to the rulers' own withheld compassion (vv2-3) or merely a natural consequence is not disambiguated by shared vocabulary within this base extract — named as a structural, not formally Q12-anchored, parallel.
- The specific building projects referred to at v10 ("who build Zion with blood") are not detailed.
- This passage's own further significance elsewhere in the prophetic corpus (v12 is, per the wider canon, later cited as evidence of Micah's own authentic prophetic status) is not supplied by this base extract's own data — named as a forward-pointer, not imported from outside knowledge.
